Legal draft

Terms of Service

A SaaS terms outline awaiting legal and commercial approval.

DRAFT — requires professional legal review.

Not attorney-approved. Final wording and organisation details must be approved before broad public launch.

The short version

O-IBS is preparing for early access / closed beta. Plan details and pricing are provisional. Check business and tax information before relying on it; AI can make mistakes. Important changes require approval. These draft terms are not a final contract.

For a practical explanation, read AI & Data Use. The full draft below still needs professional review.

Parties and scope

The contracting entity and approved business details must be inserted before these terms can be offered for acceptance. This draft separates use of the public website from subscription and application services. It is not a final contract.

Accounts and authorised access

The final terms must set out eligibility, account creation, invitations, verification, authorised users and the responsibilities of account holders. This website does not provide registration, authentication or access to business records.

Subscriptions, trials and plan entitlements

Plan names and workflow descriptions are provisional. Final pricing, VAT treatment, billing periods, trial duration, renewal, cancellation and applicable limits require business approval and verification against the application’s entitlement definitions.

Customer data and confidentiality

Review provisions about business data, appropriate access, permitted use, intellectual property, confidentiality and the relationship to the privacy notice. Define responsibilities for customer and supplier information without assuming an unreviewed legal allocation.

AI assistance and user review

Describe the scope and limits of Bizzy and assisted document extraction. Users should review uncertain information and prepared actions. Financial and business-changing actions require confirmation before completion. Final wording must be consistent with released functionality.

Acceptable use and security

The approved agreement should describe permitted use, restrictions, account security, suspension and incident reporting. No current support address or suspension process is invented here.

Support, availability and changes

Confirm actual support channels, service availability arrangements, maintenance and how material changes are communicated. This draft makes no uptime, certification or support-response guarantee.

Ending the service and data handling

Review cancellation, termination, export, deletion, backup retention and outstanding payment obligations. Verify these provisions against implemented workflows before publishing them.

Liability, disputes and governing law

A qualified professional must finalise liability, warranties, dispute handling and governing law in the context of the contracting entity and the service. No attorney-approved agreement is represented by this outline.

Approved contact details

An operational O-IBS privacy address has not been configured. Approved contact details and a request process will be added before release.
